title: Deciding when the clock is short
outcomes: Records his pace on one item and sets a half-time limit from it
Lists the opponent's checks and captures after his move in a short look, and says what the look can miss
Solves a short set at half time and names the loop step he skipped
Writes a weekly half-time set with a first target to test

steps.text: When the clock runs short, mistakes change. A pattern players and coaches report, not measured here: with little time you check the opponent's reply less and lean on the first idea. You can test this on yourself. Start a timer now and solve the next position at your usual pace; this is your baseline.

steps.prompt: Write the seconds you took, counted up to your first move. Half of that is your limit for each position in the half-time set (a set solved in half your usual time); use at least 10 seconds if half is less. The app does not run a countdown: use a timer, and when it rings play the move you have. One item is only a rough baseline, and a quick wrong answer gives a small limit.

fields.label: Seconds I took on the item:
Half of that, my limit per position:

steps.title: What a short look finds
steps.prompt: You have about ten seconds. The look is one question: after my move, what can the opponent do with a check, a capture or a threat? In the first position the capture was safe. Predict what the look finds in this one, then check.

steps.text: **What a short look can do.** A short look can list the opponent's checks and captures after your move; their threats take longer. Ten seconds is a first guess, not a tested figure. Rule of thumb, not tested here: with little time keep the look and play the simpler move; do not start a calculation you cannot finish. Next: four positions at your limit, with no hints or engine line.

steps.prompt: Four positions cannot show a pattern; use them as a first look. Name what happened. Without an untimed score on the same positions you cannot say time caused a mistake; the weekly set below adds one. A second set of four follows: keep your limit for it too, and treat a yes/no answer you guessed as a miss.

fields.label: Positions I got wrong or rushed (of four):
Did I stay within my limit?

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** The app takes hints and the engine line away but has no countdown: the limit is yours. On find-the-move items an engine check follows a move outside the list; do not count that wait. It does not read your game clocks. Nothing here shows half-time sets carry over. When you can name the step you skip, drop this page.

steps.prompt: Plan one half-time set for this week. A first target to test (from the skill node): at half time, score at least 80% of what you score at your usual pace on the same kind of positions.

fields.label: Correct at my usual pace (do this set first, untimed):
If I have less than 30 seconds in a game I will:
